name: DocVQA
description: A dataset for Visual Question Answering on document images consisting of 50,000 questions defined on 12,767 document images of varied types and content.
creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
citeAs: Mathew, Minesh; Karatzas, Dimosthenis; Jawahar, C.V. DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images. arXiv:2007.00398v3, 2021.
rai:dataCollection: Document images were sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The authors downloaded documents from different collections and hand picked pages for use in the dataset, prioritizing pages with tables, forms, lists and figures and trying to minimize binarized images because poor image quality was not desired to be a bottleneck for VQA. Questions and answers on the selected document images were collected with the help of remote workers using a web-based annotation tool in three stages: first, workers defined at most 10 question-answer pairs per image and could add more than one ground truth answer; second, another worker answered the questions and assigned one or more question types, with an option to flag inapt questions; third, cases with answer mismatch between stages were reviewed by the authors, who could edit and accept or ignore them.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in the UCSF Industry Documents Library. The final set of images are drawn from pages of 6,071 industry documents spanning 1900 to 2018 and covering five industries: tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel and chemical.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors hand picked pages from downloaded documents, tried to minimize binarized images, and prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages with only running text. The data was split randomly in an 80-10-10 ratio into train, validation and test splits.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Workers were instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. Questions flagged in stage 2 as inapt owing to language issues or ambiguity were not included in the dataset. If answers from stage 1 and stage 2 did not match exactly, the question was sent to a third-stage review by the authors, where questions and answers could be edited before acceptance.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was organized in three stages using remote workers. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it, with encouragement to add more than one ground truth answer when warranted. Workers were instructed to ask questions answerable using text present in the image and to enter the answer verbatim from the document. In stage 2, a worker was shown the image and the questions from stage 1, but not the answers, and was required to enter answers and assign one or more question types to each question. Workers could also flag questions as invalid due to language issues or ambiguity, and such questions were excluded. In stage 3, questions whose stage 1 and stage 2 answers did not match exactly were reviewed by the authors, who could edit questions and answers and then accept or ignore them.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The second stage verified data collected in the first stage. If none of the answers entered in the first stage matched exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the question was sent for review in a third stage. In the third stage, the authors reviewed mismatch cases and either accepted the question-answer after editing if necessary or ignored it. Questions flagged in stage 2 for language issues or ambiguity were not included in the dataset.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Up to 10 question-answer pairs per document image in stage 1; each question was answered again by one worker in stage 2, and mismatch cases were reviewed by the authors in stage 3.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Remote workers were used for question-answer collection and verification; human performance on the test split was measured with help of a few volunteers from the authors' institution.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The documents originate from five industries and span many decades. The paper notes that top non-numeric answers include named entities such as names of people, institutions and places.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and task aim to inspire a purpose-driven approach in document image analysis and recognition research, driving methods that use low-level cues such as text, layout and arrangements together with high-level goals such as purpose, relationship and domain knowledge in solving problems of practical importance.
rai:dataBiases: The authors prioritized non-binarized images and pages with tables, forms, lists and figures, and used many documents from food and nutrition related collections because they had a good number of non-binarized images. Most documents are from the 1960-2000 period.
rai:dataLimitations: Majority of documents in the source library are binarized and binarization has affected image quality. The authors tried to minimize binarized images because poor image quality could be a bottleneck for VQA. The paper also reports that OCR errors can lead to wrong answers even when models ground questions correctly, and that existing models need to improve specifically on questions where understanding document structure is crucial. The authors note that better understanding of figures, text on photographs, and better handwriting recognizers are needed.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Visual Question Answering on document images and for evaluating DocVQA methods and baseline models. It is split into train, validation and test sets in an 80-10-10 ratio: train has 39,463 questions and 10,194 images, validation has 5,349 questions and 1,286 images, and test has 5,188 questions and 1,287 images.
